h: Haggis, History and a Bit of Healthy Rivalry
p: Edinburgh takes its fun seriously. This is the city of the famous August festivals, a legendary Hogmanay street party and a nightlife scene that runs from candlelit whisky bars to sticky-floored student haunts. A games bar slots right into that mix, giving groups an easy way to kick off the evening without any arguments about where to go.

Getting around is easy. Waverley station sits right in the middle of the city, between the Old Town and the New Town, and the trams run from the airport through the centre to Leith and Newhaven. Buses go almost everywhere, which helps when the night runs late.

A few local tips. Edinburgh is hilly and the streets are often cobbled, so wear shoes you can walk in, especially if you're heading between venues. Weekend evenings get busy with visitors and celebration groups, so booking is a must. And in August, when the festivals are on, the city is absolutely packed, so plan everything well ahead and expect crowds everywhere.

For something to do before or after, Leith is worth the trip, with its waterfront restaurants and the former royal yacht Britannia moored at Ocean Terminal. Dean Village, a pretty little corner along the Water of Leith, feels like a world away from the busy streets despite being so close to the centre. And the Scottish National Gallery on the Mound is free to visit and perfect for a calmer hour or two.
